sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in South Carolina?
sections.html:
You record it with the register of deeds, or with the clerk of court in counties that are not listed in SC Code 30-5-10(A). In those unlisted counties the clerk performs the register's duties with the same powers. Berkeley and Dorchester registers serve four-year terms.

South Carolina has 46 counties, so which office you need depends on where the land lies. Charleston, Greenville, Richland and Horry are among the counties with a register of deeds.

sections.h2: What must happen before a deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
The deed has to be proved or acknowledged first, and 30-5-30 allows three routes. Pick the one your closing attorney uses.

  • An affidavit from a subscribing witness
  • Compliance with the Uniform Recognition of Acknowledgments Act, or a signer's affidavit that the signature is theirs
  • The grantor's acknowledgment before an officer, witnessed by two witnesses

Deeds and mortgages executed after July 1, 1976 must include a derivation clause and the grantee's mailing address, and a clerk may not record one lacking the derivation clause unless the information was unavailable (30-5-35). Quitclaim and non-warranty deeds are exempt from the clause. Leaving something out does not by itself affect validity or record notice (30-5-35(c)).

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a South Carolina deed?
sections.html:
The deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500, or fractional part of $500, of the property's value (SC Code 12-24-10). It splits into a state share and a county share.

Part of the feePer $500
State$1.30
County$0.55
Total$1.85

On a deed valued at $200,000 that is 400 units of $500, so the statutory fee is $740. The state share is credited $0.10 to the Heritage Land Trust Fund, $0.20 to the South Carolina Housing Trust Fund and $1.00 to the general fund (12-24-90). The county share goes to the county general fund. The register may also charge separate filing fees, so ask the office for a current schedule.

sections.h2: What is the affidavit of value?
sections.html:
The clerk or register must require an affidavit showing the realty's value, signed by a responsible person connected with the transaction who states that connection (12-24-70(A)(1)). The clerk may waive it at discretion. Bring the closing statement figure.

For an exempt deed, value is not required, but the affidavit must state why the deed is exempt (12-24-70(A)(2)). A willfully false affidavit is a misdemeanor with a fine up to $1,000, up to one year in prison, or both (12-24-70(C)).

sections.h2: Which deeds are exempt from the fee?
sections.html:
12-24-40 lists fifteen exemptions. The ones sellers meet most often are listed here:

  • Realty valued at $100 or less
  • Transfers to the federal government, a state or its political subdivisions, including school districts
  • Transfers where no gain or loss is recognized under IRC Section 1041
  • Corrective or quitclaim deeds confirming title already vested, with no consideration
  • Deeds in lieu of foreclosure or deeds under foreclosure proceedings to the mortgagee
  • Transfers from an agent to the principal whose funds bought the realty, with a notarized document establishing the relationship

Treat any other transfer as taxable until the register says otherwise.

sections.h2: How quickly is a deed recorded and what do you get back?
sections.html:
The register records writings in the order they are lodged, and each must be recorded within thirty days of lodgment, with the recording bearing the lodgment date (30-5-90). The register or deputy endorses a certificate showing the time, book and page. No fee is charged for that certificate (30-5-200).

Certified copies are issued on application, with fees paid in advance if required (30-5-20). Order one after closing for your files.

sections.h2: Who is responsible if the fee is not collected?
sections.html: The grantor is liable for the fee, and the grantee is secondarily liable (12-24-20). For master-in-equity deeds and deeds from the federal government, a state or its political subdivisions, the grantee is liable instead. A person who fails to pay can face a $50 to $500 penalty per failure, and a clerk who fails to collect faces the same range (12-24-120).

sections.h2: What should you bring to record a deed?
sections.html:
Bring the original signed deed, the proof or acknowledgment, the affidavit of value or exemption, the grantee's mailing address and payment for the fee. Estate deeds add one more item: a deed of distribution is how a personal representative passes real property to a distributee (62-3-907(A)), so bring the letters too.

A joint tenant's survivor files a certified death certificate with the register of deeds (27-7-40(b)).

Sellers working with Cash Home Buyers do not need to organize any of this alone. The closing attorney or title company usually records the deed, and we can walk you through it.

sections.h2: What if the deed is lodged in the wrong county?
sections.html:
South Carolina has a provision for transferring a recording to the correct county (30-5-100). Check the county before you lodge anything, because a recording in the wrong place delays the sale record and can hold up your buyer's title policy.

The county is the one where the land sits. A house near a county line is worth confirming against the tax bill.

sections.h2: Does the deed need a plat or a land use plan?
sections.html:
A land development or land use plan is not required before a deed for undeveloped land, though a local entity may still require a plat when the deed is recorded (30-5-30(D)). For a lot split or a deed of part of a parcel, call the planning office in the county or city before you head to the register.

An instrument is also not denied record because the probating officer left out a service serial number (30-5-50).

sections.h2: How does the value on the deed affect the fee?
sections.html:
The fee is set by the value of the realty, determined under 12-24-30, and counted in $500 units with any fraction rounding up. Here is how the statutory fee scales:

Stated value$500 unitsStatutory fee at $1.85
$100,000200$370
$200,000400$740
$350,000700$1,295

These figures are straight arithmetic from the per-$500 rate in 12-24-10. They leave out any separate filing charge the office sets.

sections.h2: What does recording look like for an estate or foreclosure deed?
sections.html:
Deeds that come out of an estate or a foreclosure follow the same recording steps, with different fee treatment. A deed in lieu of foreclosure, or a deed to the mortgagee under foreclosure proceedings, is on the exemption list (12-24-40(13)). A master-in-equity deed shifts liability for the fee to the grantee (12-24-20), which matters to a buyer at a foreclosure sale.

A deed of distribution from a personal representative is recorded like any other deed, and our probate page covers how that instrument works. For an estate deed, the register will still ask for an affidavit stating either the value or the exemption.

sections.h2: Why does an unrecorded deed cause trouble at a sale?
sections.html:
A buyer's title search reads the public record, and a deed that never reached the register does not appear there. Sellers who inherited a house or took title years ago sometimes find an older deed was signed but never recorded, which has to be fixed before a clean sale. The statute makes recording an orderly process, with deeds taken in the order lodged, so lodging the missing deed early starts that clock.

If you find a gap, call the register of deeds or the clerk of court in the county and ask what they need. A closing attorney can help sort it out.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording fee in South Carolina?
faqs.a: $1.85 per $500 of value or fraction, made up of $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county (12-24-10, 12-24-90). Other filing fees are set by the office.

faqs.q: Do I record at the courthouse or with the register of deeds?
faqs.a: It depends on the county. In counties not listed in 30-5-10(A), the clerk of court does the register's job.
The statute requires recording within thirty days of lodgment, in the order lodged (30-5-90).

faqs.q: Does a deed need witnesses in South Carolina?
faqs.a: Often yes. Acknowledgment before an officer is witnessed by two witnesses, but a subscribing witness affidavit is another route (30-5-30).

faqs.q: Do I need to record a deed at all?
faqs.a: Recording gives the public record the deed belongs in, and the statute sets the process once an instrument is lodged. Ask a closing attorney about priority questions.
